chunk_map.heading: A skill's footprint is where its job lands

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a reader stalls on a pronoun/name with no antecedent. Walked every chunk's referents under sequential read. Chunk1 'You drew a control loop' (L3) and chunk6 'The checking loop' (L25) are arc-earned: `the-whole-map.md` L36 already names 'THE CHECKING LOOP' as a ghost on the M2 engine map ('◌ THE CHECKING LOOP', 'read · judge · gate what ships · by hand for now'), and chunk6's figure un-ghosts that same element (maintainer L88) -- carve-out 'arc-earned spine vocabulary' covers both. Chunk2 L11 'The checks you built are the instruments inside it' resolves against the training's verifier/judge/gate practice built across M4-M5 (maintainer L149 in the sibling exercise file names the M5 vocabulary this bridges from) and against the module-arc carve-out (this lecture sits directly after exercise spot-gaps-build-the-loop per the module's deck order at spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L106) -- not a stalled referent either way. Chunk7 header 'Loop instead of you starting' (L30) uses 'the loop' -- the rule's own carve-out example lists 'the loop' by name as arc-earned spine vocabulary. Chunk4/5 'Dino Repo' / 'Pocock' (L17, L21) are first-mention proper nouns introducing new figures, not backward-pointing referents -- the rule targets assumed-known referents, not new names given explanatory content in the same beat. Chunk8's 'the pier' (L42) is a labelled element on that same chunk's figure (maintainer L66: 'the mapped next move at the pier'), same-chunk resolution. Chunk9's 'a pilot' (L48) was drawn into chunk8's figure the immediately-preceding slide (maintainer L66: 'the under-drawn pilot'), same-file adjacent-slide reuse -- not a violation.

Harm: a callback whose target depends on deck-start position. No chunk points at another file by position (no 'the opening lecture said', 'the prework at the top', etc.) anywhere in body lines 1-50. The maintainer block's own cross-file provenance notes (e.g. L82 'from the-loop-has-a-name.md') are authoring history, not student-facing text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did' resolving to a beat the current module set no longer has. Only candidate is chunk2 L11 'The checks you built' -- a class-level callback (the student's verifier/judge/gate practice across M4-M5), not a single named beat, so there is no one dead beat to strand. spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md (the exercise immediately before this lecture in M6 deck order, L106) itself works with 'a sharper existing verifier' (L114) and rule-cutting, so the callback lands on live, current-module material either way.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. 5 of 9 chunks are header+figure only (chunks 1,3,4,5,6 at L3-5,13-15,17-19,21-23,25-28) with no bullets. Each carries a dated maintainer accept-note asserting the figure alone is self-carrying and instructing 'Do not add bullets': L53 (control-loop), L55 (Dino Repo / Pocock figures, 'No bodies owed'), L86 (checking-loop-drawn-solid). Non-blocking rule regardless; accepted with note.

Harm: header states something the chunk's own content contradicts. Claim-style headers checked against their bullets: chunk2 'Eval' + its 3 bullets define eval/yardstick/checks-as-instruments, consistent; chunk7 'Loop instead of you starting' + bullets (3 scheduling primitives that run without a manual start, then the compounding-value line) match the header's claim; chunk8 'A skill's footprint is where its job lands' + bullets (footprint sizes vary: single fix / a leg / the pier, sized by the job) match exactly, and maintainer L74 confirms it as the intended thesis-claim. Figure-only chunks (1,3,4,5,6) are covered by rule 5's accept-notes asserting figure/header match; no chunk's content contradicts its header.

Harm: a cadence tic reads as filler/hollow rigour on a dense slide. Checked all 6 sub-shapes across every chunk with bullets (2,7,8,9): no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no self-grading superlative; no number-with-retraction; no abstraction-noun stack ('bounded-window reality' style); no empty-leg verb triplet. Closest candidate to an anaphora triple is chunk8 L42 'One move takes a single fix at a turning point. Another carries a whole leg. A third runs at the pier, before the first leg.' -- stays inside the rule because each leg adds distinct NEW concrete content (a fix / a leg / the pier before the first leg), not a repeated phrase carrying nothing new on the third beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold sprawl trains readers to stop attending to it. `grep -n '\*\*' curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` restricted to body lines 1-50 -> exactly 2 hits: L9 '**eval**' (Eval slide, ~5-char handle) and L41 '**skill**' (footprint slide, ~5-char handle), 1 handle per slide, both within the handle cap. Matches the maintainer's own emphasis-budget note verbatim (L59: 'bold = handles only: eval on the Eval slide, skill on the footprint slide; pilot stays plain').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a phase-less prose section renders in long-read but drops from the composed Slides deck. `site/layouts/curriculum.js` L1317-1321 wraps a standalone lecture file's whole body in the `.phase--lecture` wrapper by file kind ('exercise'|'lecture'), and `buildDeckModel` (site/layouts/slides.js L258) selects `.phase--lecture, .phase--exercise` -- so unlike a module file with unwrapped Prework/Supplementary sections, this lecture's entire body (all 9 `##` chunks) sits inside the one wrapper with nothing phase-less to drop. Ran `node scripts/slides.test.js` this session: 47/47 pass, confirming the deck-composition/anchor mechanism this reasoning relies on is intact. Diff since last audit (289b45a3) touched only prose (header rename, bullet swap) and no tier/wrapper markers, so nothing moved a chunk relative to the wrapper.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer ('below', 'above', 'the top of this page') aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at `##`. `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` -> 'OK -- 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Confirmed by hand: `grep -n -iE '\b(below|above|further down|a few paragraphs|at the top|see below|the top of this)\b' curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` -> 0 hits.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide too dense to read at presentation pace. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` -> 'files: 1  slides: 9  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets ... oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a label-style header in a lecture skips the claim beat the file's own grammar promises. This is a lecture file, so headers should be claims or NOT-violation catalogue/orientation entries. 'You drew a control loop' (L3) and 'A skill's footprint is where its job lands' (L36) are clear thesis-claims (maintainer L74 confirms the latter by name). 'Eval' (L7), 'The second loop' (L13), 'Dino Repo's skill stack' (L17), 'Pocock's skill system' (L21), 'The checking loop, drawn solid' (L25) are catalogue entries naming their subject -- the rule's own explicit non-violation class ('Ralph', 'The numbers'). 'Loop instead of you starting' (L30) reads as a claim about mechanism (the loop runs without a manual start). Closest call: 'From skills to a workflow' (L44) is a topic label rather than a stated claim -- but the maintainer block addresses this exact header by name (L74: 'names the composition concept the slide teaches in its variety'), reading it as a catalogue/transition header for the deck's closing variety-slide, consistent with the rule's own catalogue carve-out. Non-blocking regardless of the call.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that reads as rigour but adds nothing the slide doesn't already hold. Checked every bullet (chunks 2,7,8,9, 9 bullets total) against the three classes. None are doctrine restatement (each states a new move/definition, not a re-announced law -- e.g. L34's compounding line is the scheduled-loop-specific instantiation of the accumulation idea, not a repeat of it: chunk3's figure carries the general 'same surround' claim, L34 states what happens when THAT loop is left running unattended and fed its own output). None are self-referential design commentary (no 'you encounter this before we name it' framing). None are aphorism kickers restating their own header (L34 does not restate 'Loop instead of you starting'; L49 does not restate 'From skills to a workflow').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a header rename changes the slide's job but the old body keeps doing the old job, reading as a duplicate. This is the rule's own named worked example (rule text cites 'composing-the-workflow.md 2026-09-03' directly). `git diff 289b45a3..HEAD -- curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` shows the fix landed: the two inherited bullets from the-loop-has-a-name.md ('Three places this fits naturally...' / 'The skill defines the check. The runtime supplies the cadence...') are removed and replaced with 'Left running, the loop squashes the recurring things. Add what each run taught to the kit, and the same loop starts cracking harder work.' (now L34). Current chunk7 (L30-34) matches the maintainer's own description of the intended fix (L98, L100-101 Watch-for note) exactly: the surviving first bullet (three scheduling primitives, unchanged by the diff) plus this one new line is what the header 'Loop instead of you starting' owes. Covering the header and reading only the body confirms neither remaining bullet answers a DIFFERENT header's job.
